title: Console scope fence: prioritize trimmed dashboards + phased tracing/cost rollout
creator: Ananya Patel
description:
Summary:
This ticket defines a deliberate scope fence and acceptance criteria for the first public iteration of Console observability focused on three surfaces: dashboards, tracing, and per-route cost breakdowns. Objective is to ship a narrow, high-value MVP that demonstrably improves incident diagnosis and cost visibility for early customers while deferring lower-value/expensive features to Phase 2.

What we are delivering in Phase 1 (trimmed list):
- Dashboards: 3 curated cards: Route latency P50/P95, Error rate (5m rolling), Recent heavy-cost routes (top 10 by token spend). Cards are templated, not fully customizable. No ad-hoc chart builder.
- Tracing: Lightweight sampled traces at 1% default with a UI panel to view single-trace timelines and a searchable trace ID. No distributed trace joins, no flamegraphs in Phase 1.
- Cost breakdowns: Aggregate cost per-route for last 24h / 7d / 30d surfaced as top-10 table rows with inline cost delta vs prior period. Per-token drilldown and per-tenant chargebacks deferred.

Scope explicitly excluded from Phase 1 (MVP cuts):
- Full trace waterfall with span-level expand/collapse and flamegraphs.
- Free-form dashboard creation and query language.
- Real-time streaming cost microbreakdowns (per-token timestamps).
- Deep integrations with billing (chargeback exports) and role-based visibility rules beyond basic org/admin.

Why these choices?
- Shipping a small set of high-ROI cards reduces implementation complexity (frontend and backend aggregation), speeds QA, and gives clear acceptance metrics.
- Tracing joins and flamegraphs are engineering-heavy features that block launch; sampling + single-trace view will cover most debugging flows for 70% of early incidents.
- Cost drilldowns are deferred because token-level joins to model runtime metadata require schema work and can be added safely in Phase 2 without blocking core observability value.

Operational constraints and SLOs:
- Dashboard API endpoints must respond < 200ms median for cached views and < 800ms for uncached aggregation queries under standard load (see ENG-22110 for load profile).
- Trace store retention for Phase 1: 7 days.

Acceptance test notes and manual QA flows are included below. Links to mocks, PRD doc, acceptance checklist, and implementation tickets are attached in links.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard: Three cards render for a test org with 10 routes and realistic traffic within 2 clicks of Console homepage
Dashboard performance: cached card render median latency < 200ms in 95% of synthetic runs defined by ENG-22110
Tracing: Ability to view an individual sampled trace by trace ID and inspect span timestamps and logs; sample rate configurable to 0.1% / 1% / 5% via admin toggle
Cost table: Top 10 routes by token spend displayed with absolute cost and % delta vs prior period; numbers match offline billing export for test dataset within 1% tolerance
Security & access: Only org admins can change tracing sample rate or view cost exports in Phase 1
Docs: Quickstart explainer and 1-page troubleshooting playbook published to internal docs with links to where teams should file Phase 2 feature requests
decisions: Cut ad-hoc dashboard builder: will be introduced in Phase 2 after telemetry of card usage informs which templates are necessary
Trace flamegraphs postponed: enable single-trace time-series view now and prioritize storage/ingest improvements for Phase 2
Top-10 cost table only: granular per-token breakdown gated behind billing schema work (ENG-22345)
tradeoffs: User flexibility vs time-to-market: limiting dashboard customization reduces user control but accelerates delivery and reduces backend complexity
Trace depth vs storage cost: shallow sampling reduces storage and cost risk at the expense of some debug visibility
Accuracy vs MVP scope: cost numbers are aggregate and near-real-time; exact per-invoice chargeback will be built later
